finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches any user-supplied http/https URL with only a scheme check, enabling SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata, with response body reflected (first 200 chars) and redirects followed.

trace.note: returns urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host/IP check
requests.get(url) with default allow_redirects=True; body[:200] returned to caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist only (validators.py:7). No hostname, IP, port, or redirect validation. Default redirect-following enabled.

verdict.guard_found: Only validators.py:7 is_http_url, which checks the scheme alone (urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https")). views.py:20 applies that check before the sink. No hostname, IP, or port validation exists on the /fetch2 path, and requests.get at views.py:22 uses the default allow_redirects=True. The stricter is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The url comes from request.args at views.py:19 with no authentication, the only gate is the scheme-only is_http_url at views.py:20 (validators.py:7), and requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 follows redirects and returns .text[:200], so an attacker can reach internal hosts or cloud metadata.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the hostname's resolved IPs in is_safe_url, but requests.get re-resolves the hostname at views.py:14, so a DNS-rebinding attacker can return a public IP for the check and a private/metadata IP for the fetch.

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo(hostname) — first DNS lookup, result not reused
requests.get(url, allow_redirects=False) — second independent DNS lookup; response body returned

finding.guards_checked: Resolved-IP blocklist (validators.py:14-17); allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) blocks redirect-based bypass only. No IP pinning between check and connect.

verdict.guard_found: Resolved-IP blocklist at validators.py:14-17 (is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved) and scheme check at validators.py:12. Neither closes the finding: the IP blocklist is a resolve-then-check that is not reused for the connection, and the scheme check is scheme-only. views.py:14 allow_redirects=False blocks only redirect-based bypass. No exact hostname allowlist or anchored match exists.
verdict.reason: The url comes straight from request.args at views.py:11 with no authentication, is_safe_url at validators.py:10-18 resolves the hostname via getaddrinfo at line 14 and discards the result, and requests.get at views.py:14 performs an independent DNS lookup, so a rebinding hostname can pass the check and fetch a private IP.

finding.claim: is_safe_url's private-address check omits 100.64.0.0/10 (CGNAT / shared address space), so hostnames resolving to e.g. 100.100.100.200 (Alibaba Cloud metadata) pass validation and are fetched by /fetch.

trace.note: getaddrinfo resolves hostname to 100.100.100.200 (or another 100.64/10 address)
is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved all False for 100.64.0.0/10 per CPython ipaddress source (not runtime-verified; sandbox denied python execution)
requests.get fetches the CGNAT/metadata address; body returned

finding.guards_checked: is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local, is_reserved (validators.py:16). is_global not checked. Impact limited to environments with metadata/internal services in 100.64.0.0/10.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is validators.py:16 (is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local, is_reserved), which does not cover 100.64.0.0/10. There is no hostname allowlist or full-string match anywhere in views.py:9-14 or validators.py:10-18. The /fetch2 route (views.py:17-22) is a scheme-only check and is a separate, unguarded sink.
verdict.reason: validators.py:14-18 resolves the hostname and rejects only the four listed IP classes, and views.py:11-14 passes the query-string URL to requests.get after that check. A literal ?url=http://100.100.100.200/ or a hostname resolving into 100.64.0.0/10 is accepted, because CPython's ipaddress reports is_private, is_loopback, is_link_local, and is_reserved as False for that range (I'm relying on CPython's ipaddress source, not a runtime check, since I could only read files in this directory). The impact depends on whether the deployment has metadata or internal services in 100.64.0.0/10.
